decisions.reason: Because cutting and creasing sits squarely in the firm's postpress knowledge base, management can learn from early use and refine sales and service with relatively low risk.

Although UV spot varnishing broadens the portfolio and had a prominent launch, it is more distant from the firm's core know-how and has little visible market feedback yet, so it is the most exposed but still worth retaining for now.
As a sheet preparation module that directly complements existing finishing lines, it fits the firm's absorptive capacity and can be supported through established application and service routines.
The B2-format multifinisher aligns with the firm's automation direction and core finishing competence, and its prominent launch indicates enough strategic commitment to continue.
A hybrid saddle stitcher builds on established booklet-making and binding expertise, making it easier for the firm to interpret customer results and support adoption.
The folding add-on is very close to the firm's installed base and already has a named customer application, which provides concrete learning and makes withdrawal unlikely.
